title: Контракт Баринова спасает Дениса  (Barinov's Contract Saves Denis)

segments.t: On his way out of the hotel, Chef Barinov learns that Eleonora just fired Denis—and immediately storms back to invoke a clause in his contract stating that only the head chef can hire or fire cooks. Listen to the showdown.
Ты никого не уволишь из моей команды.
По контракту только я могу увольнять.
Ты сказал, что не будешь работать.
Пусть он сообщит об этом лично.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'And where are you going right now?' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'to go' without extra filler words. Chef Barinov answers right away.
'Into our happy future.' The meaning hinges on 'our' working together with 'future' in spoken Russian.
'They just fired me.' The meaning hinges on 'me' working together with 'fired' in spoken Russian.
'Well, there you go, it has started already.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'it started', turning the action back on the subject.
'Who fired you?' Chef Barinov addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'fired'.
'The hotel owner, Eleonora Andreevna.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'landlady' before landing on 'proper name'.
'That is my ex-wife's name.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'so' and 'is called' in a few short words.
'Nobody is going to fire you here.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'nobody' and finishing on 'will fire'.
'Why did you not like Denis?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'than' before landing on 'liked'.
'I actually liked him very much.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'he' and finishing on 'liked'.
'But he does not know how to cook.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'but' before landing on 'to cook'.
Ты никого не уволишь из моей команды.
'You will not fire anyone from my team.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'you' and finishing on 'commands'.
По контракту только я могу увольнять.
'Under the contract, only I can fire cooks.' Notice how Russian expresses 'according to' and 'to fire' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Eleonora answers right away.
Ты сказал, что не будешь работать.
'You said you would not work for me.' Eleonora addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'to work'.
'It was your husband who hired me.' In Russian, the idea of 'this' flows naturally into 'hired' without extra filler words.
Пусть он сообщит об этом лично.

'Let him inform me of that in person.' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'let', while 'personally' completes the thought. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Ты никого не уволишь из моей команды.
По контракту только я могу увольнять.
Ты сказал, что не будешь работать.
Пусть он сообщит об этом лично.
And that brings Chef Barinov roaring back to defend his kitchen brigade. Notice how he uses his contract with Eleonora's late husband to trump her authority. See you next time.
Денис, быстро иди работать на кухню!
